points.title: 艺术启蒙
points.description: 蒙德里安出生于荷兰阿姆斯特丹的一个艺术世家。他的父亲是小学教师，同时也是一位业余艺术家。蒙德里安从小就展现出艺术天赋，在家庭环境中接受了早期的艺术教育。这一时期，他主要跟随父亲学习绘画技巧，并开始接触荷兰传统绘画风格，特别是风景画。这段经历为他后来的艺术发展奠定了基础，同时也培养了他对自然和线条的敏感度。
points.descriptionEn: Born in Amsterdam to an artistic family, Mondrian received his early art education from his father, a primary school teacher and amateur artist. From a young age, he showed artistic talent and was exposed to traditional Dutch painting styles, particularly landscapes. This formative period laid the foundation for his later artistic development and cultivated his sensitivity to nature and lines.

points.title: 学院派探索
points.description: 蒙德里安进入阿姆斯特丹国立艺术学院学习，接受了系统的学院派艺术教育。这一时期，他的作品主要受到印象派和象征主义的影响，创作了大量风景画和静物画。1904年，他开始尝试点彩派技法，受到梵高和修拉的启发。1908年，他接触了神智学思想，开始探索艺术与精神层面的联系。1909年，他结识了荷兰先锋派艺术家巴特·凡·德·莱克，受到其现代艺术观念的影响，开始向抽象艺术转变。
points.descriptionEn: Mondrian studied at the Rijksakademie van Beeldende Kunsten in Amsterdam, receiving systematic academic art education. During this period, his works were influenced by Impressionism and Symbolism, and he produced numerous landscapes and still lifes. In 1904, he began experimenting with Pointillism techniques, inspired by Van Gogh and Seurat. In 1908, he encountered Theosophical ideas, starting to explore connections between art and spirituality. In 1909, he met Dutch avant-garde artist Bart van der Leck, whose modern art concepts influenced his shift toward abstraction.

points.title: 抽象艺术转型
points.description: 1911年，蒙德里安移居巴黎，接触到立体主义和未来主义等前卫艺术运动。在巴黎，他开始彻底改变自己的绘画风格，从具象转向抽象。1912-1913年间，他创作了《海堤》系列作品，这是他向抽象艺术过渡的重要阶段。1914年，第一次世界大战爆发，蒙德里安被迫返回荷兰，但这段巴黎经历彻底改变了他对艺术的理解，使他开始追求一种普遍的、超越个人情感的艺术表达方式。
points.descriptionEn: In 1911, Mondrian moved to Paris and encountered avant-garde art movements like Cubism and Futurism. In Paris, he began to radically transform his painting style, shifting from figurative to abstract. Between 1912-1913, he created his 'Sea Pier' series, an important transitional phase toward abstraction. When World War I broke out in 1914, Mondrian was forced to return to the Netherlands, but his Paris experience profoundly changed his understanding of art, leading him to pursue a universal, impersonal form of artistic expression.

points.title: 新造型主义萌芽
points.description: 战争期间，蒙德里安回到荷兰的莱顿，开始系统发展他的艺术理论。他结识了 Theo van Doesburg 和其他艺术家，共同创立了风格派(De Stijl)。这一时期，蒙德里安开始探索最基本的视觉元素：直线、直角和原色。1917年，他发表了《新造型主义》一文，正式提出了他的艺术理论，主张艺术应该通过最基本的几何形式和色彩来表达宇宙的和谐与平衡。这一理论成为他后来创作的基础，也影响了现代设计、建筑和艺术的发展方向。
points.descriptionEn: During the war, Mondrian returned to Leiden in the Netherlands and began systematically developing his artistic theory. He met Theo van Doesburg and other artists, co-founding the De Stijl movement. During this period, Mondrian began exploring the most basic visual elements: straight lines, right angles, and primary colors. In 1917, he published 'Neo-Plasticism,' formally presenting his artistic theory advocating that art should express cosmic harmony and balance through the most basic geometric forms and colors. This theory became the foundation for his later work and influenced the direction of modern design, architecture, and art.

points.title: 成熟与新造型主义
points.description: 1919年，蒙德里安重返巴黎，开始创作他标志性的风格：使用水平线和垂直线构成网格，填充红、蓝、黄三原色以及黑、白、灰。1925年，他与风格派成员因艺术理念分歧而分道扬镳，但继续发展自己的新造型主义理论。1938年，因纳粹威胁，蒙德里安移居伦敦，1940年又移居纽约。在纽约，他的艺术风格进一步简化，作品更加动态和富有节奏感。这一时期，他的作品对美国的抽象表现主义产生了深远影响，成为20世纪现代艺术的重要代表人物。
points.descriptionEn: Returning to Paris in 1919, Mondrian began creating his signature style: grids of horizontal and vertical lines filled with red, blue, yellow primary colors and black, white, gray. In 1925, he split from De Stijl members due to artistic differences but continued developing his Neo-Plastic theory. In 1938, fleeing Nazi threats, he moved to London, then to New York in 1940. In New York, his style further simplified, becoming more dynamic and rhythmic. During this period, his work profoundly influenced American Abstract Expressionism, establishing him as a key figure in 20th-century modern art.

appraisal.zh: 蒙德里安被公认为现代抽象艺术的奠基人之一，其新造型主义以最基本的几何形式与色彩追求普遍和谐，为极简主义、构成主义和包豪斯设计奠定了基础，红黄蓝格子更成为全球性的视觉符号。另一种看法认为，他的艺术过于理性教条，缺乏情感深度，忽视偶然性与个体表达，与当时的社会政治现实脱节，理论在实践中也易流于僵化公式。
appraisal.en: Mondrian is widely regarded as a founder of modern abstract art: his Neo-Plasticism pursued universal harmony through the most basic geometric forms and colors, laying groundwork for Minimalism, Constructivism and Bauhaus design, while his red-yellow-blue grids became a global visual symbol. Another view holds that his art was overly rational and dogmatic, lacking emotional depth, neglecting chance and individual expression, detached from the social and political realities of his time, and prone to rigidity in practice.

supporter.zh: 蒙德里安被视为现代艺术的先驱和抽象艺术的奠基人之一。他的新造型主义理论彻底改变了20世纪艺术的发展方向，为极简主义、构成主义和包豪斯设计理念奠定了基础。蒙德里安通过最基本的几何形式和色彩，创造了一种超越个人情感、追求普遍和谐的艺术语言，这种理念至今仍在设计、建筑和时尚领域产生深远影响。他的作品不仅是艺术杰作，更是现代主义精神的完美体现。
supporter.en: Mondrian is regarded as a pioneer of modern art and one of the founders of abstract art. His Neo-Plastic theory revolutionized the direction of 20th-century art, laying the foundation for Minimalism, Constructivism, and Bauhaus design principles. By creating an artistic language transcending personal emotions through basic geometric forms and colors, Mondrian established a universal pursuit of harmony that continues to profoundly influence design, architecture, and fashion today. His works are not only artistic masterpieces but perfect embodiments of the modernist spirit.

critic.zh: 批评者认为蒙德里安的艺术过于理性和教条化，缺乏情感深度和人文关怀。他的新造型主义理论被指责为过于简化艺术，忽视了艺术中的偶然性和个体表达。此外，蒙德里安对纯粹几何形式的追求被认为与当时的社会政治现实脱节，未能回应时代的动荡和变革。一些评论家还指出，他的艺术理论虽然影响深远，但在实践中往往变得僵化和公式化，限制了艺术家的创造性探索。
critic.en: Critics argue that Mondrian's art was overly rational and dogmatic, lacking emotional depth and human关怀. His Neo-Plastic theory is criticized for oversimplifying art and neglecting the role of chance and individual expression. Furthermore, Mondrian's pursuit of pure geometric forms is seen as disconnected from the social and political realities of his time, failing to respond to the era's turmoil and transformations. Some commentators also note that while his artistic theory was influential, it often became rigid and formulaic in practice, limiting artists' creative exploration.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，蒙德里安被定义为20世纪最具影响力的艺术家之一，他的作品超越了纯粹的艺术范畴，成为现代设计语言的重要组成部分。他的红黄蓝格子图案已成为全球流行的视觉符号，出现在时尚、建筑、产品设计等多个领域。蒙德里安的艺术生涯体现了从具象到抽象的转变过程，反映了现代主义艺术的核心追求：寻找普遍性和永恒性。他的影响力不仅限于艺术领域，更延伸至整个现代视觉文化，成为现代性和理性美学的标志性代表。
objective.en: In historical and popular culture contexts, Mondrian is defined as one of the most influential artists of the 20th century. His works transcend pure art to become essential components of modern design language. His red, blue, and yellow grid patterns have become global visual symbols appearing in fashion, architecture, product design, and other fields. Mondrian's artistic career embodies the transition from figurative to abstract art, reflecting modernist art's core pursuit of universality and permanence. His influence extends beyond art to the entire modern visual culture, making him an iconic representative of modernity and aesthetic rationality.

self.zh: 艺术必须超越现实，达到纯粹的表达。
self.en: Art must transcend reality and arrive at a pure expression.
